answer: One agent, one active insurance policy: a licensed insurer verifies the operator once, then signs each epoch challenge binding the policy number to the agent's key — a glacier-slow, deliberate check no swarm can rush, since every policy needs real underwriting, a real person, and a real premium. A forged or rented policy collapses at claim time, and the insurer's audit trail names every fake. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 real policies at about $120 a year each, roughly $120,000 — a cost as hard and clear as crystal, and just as hard to fake as quartz.
